prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1083; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record, if that's all right. You can refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Understood. Let's proceed. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving on a major road in Sugar Land, Texas, heading toward a shopping center where I had an errand to run.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was in the middle lane, and traffic was moving slowly. I signaled and checked my mirror to move into the right lane because my exit was coming up.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the collision?

A: Not at first. I checked my mirror, didn't see anything in that spot, and started to move over. Then I heard a loud scrape and felt my car get pushed toward the curb.

Q: Which part of your car was struck?

A: The passenger side of my car, near the rear door. The other vehicle's driver side mirror and front fender seemed to be the parts that made contact.

Q: What did you do after the vehicles came to a stop?

A: I gripped the steering wheel hard and tried to stay calm. My right wrist was throbbing, and I got out of the car when I could. I remember the other driver walking over and asking if I was okay.

Q: When did you first realize you had been hurt?

A: Honestly, I thought it was just a bad bruise at first. By the time I got home, the swelling was so bad I couldn't rotate my wrist, and I went to the emergency room that evening.

Q: What treatment have you received for the wrist?

A: They took X-rays and told me the wrist was fractured. I had a splint put on right away, and later I was referred to an orthopedic specialist. I've been going to physical therapy twice a week since then.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?

A: It's been hard. I'm right-handed, so simple things like buttoning a shirt, cooking, or typing for my job have been difficult. I had to ask my family to help with grocery shopping for a few weeks.

Q: Have you been able to return to your regular activities?

A: Not fully. I've started going back to work with some limitations, and I've stopped playing the weekend recreational tennis I used to enjoy. My doctor says recovery will take more time.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that wrist?

A: No. It had never been injured before this collision.
